steps.name: Ask
steps.leader: Staff use one approved AI tool. Company data stays under its terms.

steps.name: Gateway
steps.leader: Every call passes one gateway. It pins the model version, logs the call and stops spend at a cap.

steps.name: Read sources
steps.leader: The tool reads allowed sources, checks dates, and reads web pages in a model that cannot act.

steps.name: Agent acts
steps.leader: An agent works with its own low-privilege login. Delete, deploy or pay needs a person to approve.

steps.name: Claim check
steps.leader: A separate checker ties each claim to a quoted sentence on a page it opened. Claims it cannot back are marked.

steps.name: Named checker
steps.leader: For work that leaves the company, a named person opens the sources and figures before it is sent.

steps.name: Logged
steps.leader: Failures and cost land in the failure log and value ledger. Stop rules end what does not pay back.

always.name: Your own test set
always.leader: Runs before any model or setting change.

always.name: Contract terms
always.leader: Notice before change, pay per result, full export.

plays.label: A good answer
plays.msg: Every control passes. The answer leaves with its sources checked and the call logged.

plays.label: A planted source
plays.msg: Source lists catch known bad sites, and the checker can tick a quote that sits on a planted page. The named checker is the net that stops it.

plays.label: An unbacked figure
plays.msg: The claim check finds no sentence that backs the figure and marks it. It goes back to be fixed before anyone sees it.

plays.label: An agent overreach
plays.msg: The agent tries to delete a production table. The fence asks a person to approve, and the action is refused and logged.

Write down the intended purpose and build your own test set from data the vendor cannot see and that looks like live data.

cells.detail: Pin the model version behind the gateway and add the system to the AI inventory with its version, owners and known issues.

cells.std: EU AI Act Articles 4 and 26(7). ISO 42001 clauses 7.2 and 7.3

cells.std: NIST AI RMF GOVERN 1.5. ISO 42001 clause 9.3. US OMB M-25-22 section 4.d.iii.E

why.Contracts: Change terms at the next renewal, before anything is built on them.
why.Platform: One tool, a gateway with pinned models, your own test set.
why.Controls: Claim check, source rules and the agent fence, on the gateway.
why.People and money: Named checkers, a value ledger and the failure log.

board.s: We tracked 24 ways AI tools fail. None was fixed in the last 30 days.
Gartner survey: only 13% of CIOs say AI has brought significant or transformational value.
In one audit, over 60% of AI search citations got the article, publisher or link wrong.

AI agents acting wrongly is the one problem with harm clearly rising. Monthly incidents were 3.3 times higher in September and October than in June to August, against 1.3 times for all AI incidents logged.
Ten building blocks cover all 24 problems. Four do most of the work: a named checker, an agent fence, pinned models and contract terms.

unknowns.s: Only 12 of the 24 failures have an independent measured result, mostly in labs. None was measured inside a working company.
In lab tests, doctors missed most planted errors in AI drafts. Stop rules and off-switch drills are measured nowhere.
The cost bands are modelled from list prices for one example firm.
This is desk research. Interviews with the people who own AI have not been run.

worse.name: Harm rising
worse.s: Our count of dated harm events grew faster than AI news overall.

new.name: New events
new.s: Fresh cases appeared, but a rise in harm was not shown.

A Canadian tribunal held the airline liable for its bot, February 2024.

head: Still
unsolved

items.s: UK NCSC says it may never be fully mitigated, 8 Dec 2025
Hijack success rose from 57% to 80% over 25 tries
MCP login is optional in the 2025-06-18 spec, local servers sit outside it
Sanctions have not stopped them, 2,293 cases by 14 Nov 2026
The vendor's own evals missed the Aug 2025 bugs, customers cannot detect them

gaps.our: Our fixes shrink these risks. None of them closes the five gaps above.
